- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.3) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price unit.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–2% or 0.5–1.0 price unit to align with mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (≥ 3% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5 price units for next 3–5 days.
- Model tends to lag in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile; add 0.2–0.5 price unit bias to short-term forecasts if sentiment swings > 0.2.
- For 10+ day horizons, model often overestimates mean; apply a 0.5–1.0 price unit downward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.3 → -0.2 → +0.3), model misreads momentum; apply a 0.5–1.0 price unit correction toward prior 3-day average.
